---
title: Refund processing
department: finance
status: archived
---
This page describes how Northwind processes a customer refund once a service
failure has been agreed. It does not cover damage claims, which follow the
claims process and are settled against the declared value rather than the
freight charge.

A refund is issued against the original payment method wherever that method is
still valid. Where the card has expired or the account has closed, finance
issues a credit note against the customer account instead, and the account
manager is notified so the credit is applied to the next invoice.

A refund of the freight charge is approved automatically when a shipment misses
its committed transit by more than one full business day and no exclusion
applies. Weather, customs holds and an incorrect address supplied by the shipper
are exclusions and no automatic refund is issued.

Refunds are paid within ten business days of approval. The customer sees the
funds on their statement within a further three to five business days depending
on their bank, and finance cannot shorten that second window.

Partial refunds are used where only part of a consignment failed. The refund is
calculated pro rata on the chargeable weight of the affected packages, not on
the number of packages, because a single heavy package can carry most of the
freight charge.

A refund request older than ninety days from the delivery date is declined
automatically. The ninety day limit is contractual and support agents should not
imply that an exception is possible; exceptions require a director approval and
are recorded against the account.

Duplicate refund requests for the same shipment are closed without action. The
finance team reviews duplicates monthly, because a rising duplicate rate usually
means the refund status is not visible enough in the customer portal.
